blogs.title: Why Tokenizers Are Becoming a Bottleneck for Modern LLMs
blogs.description: An introductory post that explains the hidden costs and biases introduced by fixed‑vocabulary tokenizers, why they struggle with multilingual data, noisy inputs, and long‑tail content, and sets the stage for why a tokenizer‑free approach like the Byte Latent Transformer can be a game‑changer.

blogs.title: Byte Latent Transformer 101: From Bytes to Dynamic Patches
blogs.description: A high‑level walk‑through of the BLT architecture—how raw bytes are grouped into variable‑size patches using an entropy‑driven algorithm, the role of the lightweight local encoder/decoder, and how the global latent transformer processes these patches to allocate compute where it’s needed most.

blogs.title: Entropy‑Based Patching Explained: Letting Data Decide the Boundaries
blogs.description: A deep dive into the three patching strategies explored in the paper (static strided, whitespace, and entropy patching), focusing on how next‑byte entropy is computed, how thresholds are set, and why entropy patching yields better efficiency and performance than traditional tokenization.

blogs.title: Scaling Without Tokens: How BLT Matches Llama 3 at 8 B Parameters
blogs.description: An analysis of the flop‑controlled scaling experiments that show BLT achieving parity with token‑based LLMs while saving up to 50 % inference FLOPs. The post will cover training vs. inference budgets, the impact of larger patch sizes, and why growing both model size and patch size is now possible.

blogs.title: Robustness by Design: Byte‑Level Models Against Noisy and Low‑Resource Text
blogs.description: A user‑friendly overview of BLT’s superior robustness—covering experiments on noisy inputs (AntSpeak, random drops, case changes), character‑level tasks like G2P and CUTE, and low‑resource machine translation—highlighting why raw byte modeling improves orthographic understanding.

blogs.title: From Tokenized Giant to Token‑Free Ninja: Distilling Llama 3 into a BLT Model
blogs.description: Explains the “byte‑ify” process where BLT inherits the global transformer weights from a pretrained tokenizer‑based model, fine‑tunes only the local modules, and achieves competitive results with far fewer training FLOPs. Includes practical tips for researchers wanting to convert existing models.
